videos.title: Copilot vs Copilot Studio: What’s the Difference for Building Agents?
videos.description:
If you want to build an AI agent with Microsoft Copilot, there are two places you can do it without needing to write code: inside Copilot itself using Agent Builder, or in Copilot Studio.

They’re designed for quite different things, and knowing where one stops and the other starts will save you a lot of confusion.

In this video, I’ll show you both experiences and explain when I would use each one. We’ll start with Agent Builder in Copilot, where you can create an agent with its own instruction

videos.title: AI agents = messy roommates
videos.description:
If you run agents all day, they’re probably using your computer more than you are, opening browsers, starting services, writing files, and leaving a lot of it behind when the job is done. A faster chip and more memory help, but they won’t stop that load from growing, so before you spend money on a bigger machine it’s worth setting a few house rules for the agents already living on yours. I wrote up how I’d do that, plus the memory and storage I’d actually buy for an agent computer.
